item.title: Episode 8 | Same AI Tool, 58% More Use — The Pitch Made the Difference
item.description: Episode 8 | Same AI Tool, 58% More Use — The Pitch Made the Difference. The same AI tool, introduced differently and backed differently, can see 58% more use — and 70% more willingness to try new uses. The difference is not the tool; it is what managers say AI is for, and whether they deliver on it. This episode covers why the "productivity" pitch backfires, the LawBot two-department comparison, tight vs. loose coupling, and how to fix the metrics — plus three actions. Adapted from the column article "想让员工拥抱 AI？别再拿“提效”当卖点".

item.title: Episode 7 | Flat Org Charts, Concentrated Power?
item.description: Episode 7 | Flat Org Charts, Concentrated Power? A thinner org chart does not necessarily mean power is more dispersed. The same AI can help colleagues coordinate directly — or let fewer managers oversee more people, in finer detail. This episode covers production technology vs. organization technology (OrgTech), vertical vs. horizontal OrgTech, evidence from about 3,000 US listed companies, and three actions. Adapted from the column article "超越自动化：AI 如何改变管理本身".

item.title: Episode 6 | 80% Say AI Pays Off. Only 7% Pass the Test
item.description: Episode 6 | 80% Say AI Pays Off. Only 7% Pass the Test. 80% of managers say AI delivers a positive return, 28% a strongly positive one — yet only 7% of organizations pass all three success markers. The gap is not in the tool. It is in the organization. This episode covers the three markers and four lines of divergence: metrics, settling, workflows and accountability, and the alignment gap — plus three actions. Adapted from the column article '适应性优势：谁在靠 AI 赢，靠的是什么'.

item.title: Episode 5 | A Human in the Loop Isn't Enough
item.description: Episode 5 | A Human in the Loop Isn't Enough. Putting a human in the loop does not mean you've preserved human judgment. In the MIT Sloan × BCG expert panel, 65% agreed that preserving trustworthy human judgment will be the defining challenge of responsible AI, 19% disagreed, 15% stayed neutral. This episode covers why judgment is worth keeping, how we lose it, five recommendations, and three things to do on Monday. Adapted from the column article '在关键处保住人的判断力'.

item.title: Episode 4 | The More You Ask AI, the Less You Know Your Team
item.description: Episode 4 | The More You Ask AI, the Less You Know Your Team. The more people use AI, the more they think their colleagues are specialists — and the less they know who to ask. In teams where asking AI instead of a colleague is normal, coordination scores 22.3 percent lower and trust 21.9 percent lower. This episode covers the two costs, three reasons, and four recommendations, plus three moves for managers. Adapted from the column article 'Team Dynamics Weaken When Employees Turn to AI Instead of Colleagues'.

item.title: Episode 3 | The Agents Are Here — Who's Next in Line?
item.description: Episode 3 | The Agents Are Here — Who's Next in Line? Agents now handle code, email, booking, and deep research. The most dangerous consequence may not be how many jobs they take today, but that in ten years, nobody is ready to take over. This episode asks four questions: cheaper output or better output, whether you can trust your agent, where future leaders will come from, and where you put your values — ending with three moves you can act on. Adapted from the column article 'AI Agents Are Here. Are Leaders Ready?'

item.title: Episode 2 | Your Juniors Look Better With AI — But Are They?
item.description: Episode 2 | Your Juniors Look Better With AI — But Are They? Juniors using AI produce better work — but their craft doesn't improve once the AI is gone. A three-month MIT field experiment with 133 patent lawyers found the opposite of what you'd expect: juniors gain most with AI and least without it, while seniors gain most without it. This episode unpacks the experiment, the springboard-vs-cushion split, and three things managers can do on Monday: two scorecards, mandatory hands-on steps for juniors, and a different job for seniors. Adapted from the column article 'Does AI Assistance Enhance or Erode Expertise?' (article 112), source MIT, David Autor et al., Oct 7, 2026. Hosts: Xiaose and Marcus. Duration 12:46.

item.title: Episode 1 | 40% deploy AI, 6% profit from it
item.description: Episode 1 | 40% deploy AI, 6% profit from it. Forty percent of large companies have deployed AI agents at scale — only six percent say AI contributes more than five percent of operating profit. The gap isn't technology; it's how the company is run. This episode unpacks McKinsey's AI operating system: what it is, its four jobs, a global insurer's three-day turnaround, four differences from traditional tools, six priorities for building one, and four shifts in management itself. Ends with three things you can do on Monday. Adapted from the column article 'AI Operating System: The CEO's New Way of Running the Company' (article 111), source McKinsey, Oct 12, 2026. Hosts: Xiaose and Marcus. Duration 14:14.
